page: Vultr voc-g-40c-160gb-768s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The configuration features 40 dedicated vCPUs derived from 20 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 160.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 768 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 123,693.48 and a PassMark CPU score of 72,888.75, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, achieving top-tier read-only large block bandwidth of 451.84 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth of 262.45 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Database operations and web serving throughput align with mid-range expectations, with Redis SET operations reaching 84.31 million operations per second and static web serving throughput recorded at 34.59 GB/sec.

The server offers high resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring sustained CPU and memory bandwidth without the overhead of GPU accelerators. However, single-threaded performance is moderate, as demonstrated by average-tier gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, medium-scale web serving, and moderate LLM inference tasks, such as text generation with 7B parameter models where it achieves a strong 35.09 tokens per second.
